deep.reconstruction:
Context (cote 155, 'Rigidité de catégories tensorielles?', after 1984): this is Tannakian-style reconstruction. A category Mod(A) of modules over an algebra 𝒜 comes with a fibre/forgetful functor F, either to vector spaces or, more generally, to a base tensor category C. The question is what extra structure on 𝒜 corresponds to a rigidity (duality) on Mod(A).

Step 1. A duality M ↦ M̌ = D(M) is required to be compatible with F, meaning F(M̌) ≅ F(M)^∨. It is an (anti-)equivalence of categories, so it is exact, in particular right exact. By an Eilenberg–Watts/Morita-duality argument it must therefore be representable: D(M) ≅ Hom_𝒜(M, I) for an object I of C carrying a left 𝒜-action ('opération à gauche').

Step 2. Evaluating at M = 𝒜 gives I ≅ Hom_𝒜(𝒜, I) ≅ D(𝒜). By compatibility with F, this is Ǎ, the dual of the underlying object of 𝒜. Grothendieck calls it 𝒰. Its first 𝒜-module structure comes by transposition from right multiplication of 𝒜 on itself (𝒜_d), so 𝒰 is an 𝒜-module.

Step 3. For Hom_𝒜(−, 𝒰) to land again in Mod(𝒜), 𝒜 must also act on 𝒰 by a second action commuting with the first. So 𝒰 needs a module structure over 𝒜 ⊗ 𝒜. His parenthetical warning: these are not bilinear for the 'obvious' bi-structure on 𝒰.

Step 4. Such commuting actions correspond to algebra maps 𝒜 → End_𝒜(𝒰). Since transposition is contravariant, End_𝒜(𝒰) ≅ End_𝒜(𝒜_d)^∘ ≅ 𝒜^∘.

Conclusion. One must give an algebra map a : 𝒜 → 𝒜^∘, i.e. an anti-endomorphism u ↦ ǔ. This is the antipode, now recovered from the rigidity of Mod(𝒜). The page thus re-derives how rigidity of a fibred module category is encoded by an antipode-type anti-homomorphism (bialgebra → Hopf algebra). If 𝒜 is an algebra in a general tensor category C, this anticipates the setting of Hopf algebras in braided/monoidal categories.
errors: Gap: for D to be an anti-equivalence (involutive up to isomorphism), a must be invertible (bijective antipode). This and the compatibility of a with the tensor/coalgebra structure, which would make it a genuine antipode, are not stated on this page.
Exactness only gives representability when Mod(A) is reasonable (e.g. finite-type modules over a finite algebra, or a suitable abelian setting). The argument is sketched, not justified.
Transcription/notation ambiguity: the right-regular module is written 𝒜_d (droite) in the formula, while the transcription has 𝒜_g in the text line; the text line should probably also read 𝒜_d.

ideas.what: A contravariant exact duality on a module category compatible with the fibre functor is representable as Hom_A(−, I) with I the dual of A.
ideas.modern_name: Morita duality / Eilenberg–Watts representation of exact functors

ideas.what: Rigidity of Mod(A) compatible with the fibre functor amounts to an anti-homomorphism A → A^op (an antipode), via End_A(A^∨) ≅ A^op.
ideas.modern_name: Tannakian reconstruction of the antipode (bialgebra is Hopf iff its comodule/module category is rigid)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Saavedra Rivano (1972), Ulbrich (1990), Majid, Schauenburg, Deligne 'Catégories tannakiennes' (1990)

ideas.what: Possible setting of algebras A in a base tensor category C, with I an object of C: relative rigidity for module categories over algebras internal to C.
ideas.modern_name: Hopf algebras in (braided) monoidal categories; module categories / relative Tannaka duality

missed.claim: Evidence that Grothendieck, around or after 1984 and independently of Drinfeld's quantum-group work, was reconstructing antipodes from rigidity of tensor categories with fibre functors, possibly over a base tensor category C. The mathematics itself is now standard.
missed.quote: il faut se donner 𝒜 —a: u ↦ ǔ→ 𝒜°
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly historical: it documents Grothendieck's late return to Tannakian / tensor-category themes in parallel with the emergence of quantum groups and Hopf-algebra reconstruction.

deep.surprise_reason: A clean but standard derivation: rigidity corresponds to an antipode via a Morita-duality argument. It was known in substance (Saavedra) and systematized soon after by Ulbrich, Majid and Deligne. Only the historical context and the possibly internal-to-C setting are mildly interesting.
transcription_corrections: 'Rigidité : M → M̌' with a struck-out alternative and 'D(M)' written above; continuation reads '(compatible avec foncteurs fibres F)'.
'foncteurs équivalences de catégories, donc exact[e] / donc exact à droite' — the struck phrase is 'donc donné par', rewritten on the next line.
'muni d'opération de 𝒜 à g.' = 'à gauche'.
'I = D(𝒜) ≃ Ǎ^(𝒜) = 𝒰' with the annotation 'compatibilité avec F' under Ǎ.
'des opérations de 𝒜 à droite sur 𝒜_d' — likely 𝒜_d (right regular module), consistent with End_𝒜(𝒜_d) later.
'Il faut donc faire opérer 𝒜 à gauche sur cet objet de Mod(𝒜) (donc mettre sur 𝒰 une structure de module sur 𝒜 ⊗ 𝒜)'.
Final line: 'il faut se donner 𝒜 --a: u ↦ ǔ--> 𝒜°' (an anti-homomorphism).
